rv.q: For some members of Generation X, what this show offers will be more than enough.
As soon as you have a little distance from it, as with many an ’80s fad like crimped hair or the War on Drugs, the thing looks a lot more questionable.

As with his recent Broadway success, “Gutenberg!,” director Gordon Greenberg takes his job seriously, keeping the show moving as a fleet pace. Better still, he also never makes the show too serious, ensuring that its tongue remains firmly planted in one cheek or another almost the whole time.
The Heart of Rock and Roll offers an enjoyable and escapist night out.
Even if you’re not an admirer, “The Heart of Rock and Roll” offers more goofy grace and buoyancy than most of its peers.
To distract from this baffling tale, director Gordon Greenberg's high-energy production throws a ton of pure adrenaline at the audience.
Around the edges of this production are a few inspired performances... despite the paper-thin material.

cn.t: Critics find this energetic Huey Lewis jukebox musical delivers '80s nostalgia and sporadic laughs through committed performances and high-energy direction, but struggles with a thin, baffling plot that rarely rises above pure adrenaline and nostalgia.

vs.sum: The Bernard B. Jacobs Theatre offers excellent sightlines from most seats, though comfort is compromised by tight legroom, especially in the mezzanine. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historic architecture and unique murals, but restroom facilities are limited, leading to long lines during intermission.

acc.note: 7 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. Copper induction loop available.
